title: Inflation-Driven Nominal Yield Spike Supports USD Temporarily, But Real Yields Set the Dollar’s Fate
catalyst: Hot US inflation print fans fears of Fed rate hike as energy costs spread
content:
The latest US inflation surge, propelled by WTI crude topping $102/bbl, has pushed nominal 10-year Treasury yields to 4. 46%, reviving market expectations for Fed tightening. This inflation shock tightens the labor-inflation persistence channel, meaning nominal yields remain elevated as inflation expectations adapt upward. However, the key transmission to FX hinges not on nominal yields alone but on the direction of real yields embedded in TIPS. Real yields drive the dollar’s underlying strength or vulnerability because the USD’s sensitivity tracks real yield shifts more than nominal levels.

The mechanism runs through oil-driven headline inflation elevating Fed policy expectations and nominal yields, initially supporting the USD. Yet, historical data from crisis analogs reveal a striking negative correlation (-0. 83) between Broad Dollar YoY% and WTI YoY%, signaling that sustained high energy prices suppress real yields via growth slowdown and inflation persistence. This dynamic pressures EM carry trades: as US real yields peak or decline, carry compression sets in because EM yields fail to keep pace, leading to EM FX weakness amid USD strength fading. USD/JPY’s current modest softness alongside falling equities flags early JPY carry unwind risk due to funding pressures, a critical gauge for broader risk appetite.

We remain cautious-bearish on the broad dollar at 98. 31 DXY. While the inflation-driven nominal yield spike supports USD now, the likely peak in real yields as breakevens adjust under slowing growth paves the way for a sharp dollar reversal. This view changes if 10Y TIPS real yields hold above 1. 5% or begin rising within the next three weeks, confirming sustained USD strength despite inflation shocks.
